name: Hill Mari (Western Mari)

ancestors.notes: Mari macrolanguage node (ISO 639-3 chm); Hill/Western Mari is one of its two individual languages.

notes: Hill Mari / Western Mari (кырык мары), Mari El, Russia. INPUT CONTRACT: modern Hill Mari 35-letter Cyrillic orthography, NFC (⟨Ӓӓ Ӧӧ Ӱӱ Ӹӹ⟩ are precomposed characters). ⟨ы⟩ and ⟨ӹ⟩ are two DISTINCT reduced/high-central vowels in Hill Mari, /ə/ and /ɯ/ respectively (Kangasmaa-Minn 1998; confirmed against NorthEuraLex Segments: ышма -> ə ʃ m ɑ, сӹнзӓ -> s ɯ n z æ), unlike Meadow Mari where ⟨ы⟩ alone covers this space — the two Mari varieties are not run off the same template (AGENTS.md, 'a shared alphabet is not a shared phonology'). ⟨г⟩ defaults to the fricative /ɣ/ (Kangasmaa-Minn 1998; NorthEuraLex шӹргӹ -> ʃ ɯ r ɣ ɯ), but hardens to the stop /ɡ/ after a nasal, so the sequence ⟨нг⟩ is entered as a multigraph /ŋɡ/ — its IPA is not the concatenation of ⟨н⟩ /n/ + ⟨г⟩ /ɣ/ (NorthEuraLex онгылаш -> o ŋ g ə l ɑ ʃ). Coronal palatalisation before iotated vowels, well attested for Meadow Mari, is NOT reproduced here for Hill Mari without its own citable evidence: NorthEuraLex's Hill Mari нер is transcribed plain [n e r] (unlike Meadow Mari's palatalised [nʲ e r]), so no palatalisation digraphs are claimed pending a source that states the rule for this variety specifically. Word stress in Hill Mari is not fixed and not reliably orthography-predictable (Kangasmaa-Minn 1998); documented here as an ENGINE-LIMIT stress exemption and not modelled. ITERATION FIX (error-analysis pass against NorthEuraLex): ⟨д⟩ corrected to the voiced dental fricative /ð/, not the stop /d/ — a genuine Hill Mari lenition absent from Meadow Mari (NorthEuraLex эдем -> eðem, кид -> kið, вӹд -> vɯð; the same 'shared alphabet is not shared phonology' caution as the ⟨ы⟩/⟨ӹ⟩ split above); the default reading of ⟨е⟩ was reordered to plain /e/ first (word-initial [j]-onset only applies in narrower positional contexts than the two-candidate list previously implied); and a Latin-letter ⟨ö⟩ variant of ⟨ӧ⟩ (/ø/, appearing in some digitised Hill Mari sources that mix Latin and Cyrillic diacritics) was added.
